title: The band as a family
summary: Late breakfasts, late movies and visits from musicians like Bob Mitchell; he calls it a highlight of his career.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: This band was pretty much like a family. In fact, quite a few nights...practically every night after we finished work, we would go down on the corner to a place where we would eat breakfast and sit around and rap, and the other musicians would come...called cookers(?). The other musicians would drop by. In fact, that's where I first met Bob Mitchell, the trumpet player with Jimmie Lunceford; I met him there. I met a lot of nice fellows that used to come through there and hang every night. And then we would leave there in the wee, wee hours, and go to the Roxy Theatre on Woodward and watch the late flicks, you know!
We really had great times, that band. In fact, that was one of the highlights of my career, because we had good show music to play, good band music to play, and we had a good rapport among ourselves.
